Attached is a technical draft (redwood_iam_response_20260213_draft.pdf) with the following high-level points filled in:
- SSO: We support SAML 2.0 (SP and IdP-initiated), assertions signed; optional encrypted assertions for customers needing that. We also support OIDC (Authorization Code + PKCE for public clients).
- SAML details: Support for transient and persistent NameID, attributes mapped via admin console; SAML metadata import via admin UI or API.
- OIDC: Standard claims supported (sub, email, name, groups); token lifetimes configurable per-tenant.
- SCIM: SCIM 2.0 API endpoints (PATCH/POST/DELETE/GET). Delta sync via /Bulk and incremental via changeLog tokens. Provisioning requires a bearer provisioning token generated by tenant admin (rotatable). Error responses include details (HTTP 4xx with JSON payload) and retry recommendations.
- RBAC: Built-in roles: Organization Admin, Region Admin, Developer, Read-Only. Custom role creation via console and API; roles can be scoped to model routes.
- Admin controls: 2FA enforcement, IP allowlist for admin actions, session timeout policies.

Open items I flagged:
1) Retention window for provisioning logs — default 90 days, can be extended under Dedicated/Private contracts.
2) SCIM group-to-role mapping examples (I included two common patterns, want Steph to validate).

Please review and add notes; once Steph and Michael sign off I'll produce a PDF for Alicia.

Thanks,

Thanks Dev — the draft is in great shape. A few edits and clarifications I recommend adding before sending:

- SCIM specifics: Confirmed SCIM 2.0 with support for bulk operations and pagination. We should explicitly state support for attribute-level mappings: e.g., mapping SCIM 'members' to RBAC groups in Redwood and the default behavior on missing attributes (we do not delete roles automatically). Also call out provisioning error queue — failed operations are logged and surfaced to tenant admins; we retain those logs for 90 days by default.

- RBAC & admin controls: Clarify that we have hierarchical roles and can restrict role creation to Organization Admins. Add a short paragraph on separation of duties: billing/admin vs platform operators (we can restrict access to billing info to a finance role).

- Auditability: We record admin console changes (user invites, role grants, permission changes) with timestamp, actor email, and IP address. Audit log exports available via API and console. For customers on Dedicated/Private we can offer longer retention and log export frequency controls.

- SAML notes: For encrypted assertions we recommend AES-256; for compatibility we accept RSA-SHA256 signatures. Also mention metadata URL refresh cadence (admins can set a refresh interval; default 24h).

- Legal flag: Michael — we should confirm we can state 90-day default retention in writing or if we need to offer a configurable baseline.

If everyone is good, I'll approve the language and Rishi can send the final PDF.

-Stephanie
Senior Security Engineer

Alicia — attached is our completed questionnaire and short implementation guidance you requested. Files attached: redwood_iam_response_20260214.pdf, saml-implementation-guide.pdf

Summary highlights:
- SSO: SAML 2.0 (SP + IdP-initiated), support for RSA-SHA256 signatures and optional encrypted assertions (AES-256). OIDC supported (Auth Code + PKCE). Metadata import and automated refresh supported via admin console.
- SCIM: We expose a SCIM 2.0-compliant provisioning API with PATCH support, bulk operations, and delta sync. Provisioning requires a rotatable bearer token and supports attribute mapping (including group -> role mapping). Failure details surfaced to admins, with retries and a retention window (default 90 days; longer for Dedicated/Private).
- RBAC: Built-in roles are provided; customers can create scoped custom roles via console/API. Role creation can be restricted to Organization Admins. We support separation of duties and can restrict billing access to finance roles.
- Audit & admin controls: Admin actions logged (actor, timestamp, IP), exportable via API. Support for 2FA, IP allowlists, session timeouts.

Attachments also include a short SAML implementation guide to help your IdP team. If you want, we can schedule a 30-min technical walkthrough next week (we're available Tue/Thu mornings PST).
